sentences.text:
These appeals are filed challenging the judgment and award dated 12.10.2010 passed by the Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City (for short, 'the tribunal') in MVC.No.6006/2019.
2. MFA.No.4121/2022 is preferred by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being dissatisfied with the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, whereas MFA No.227/2022 is preferred by the Corporation seeking to set-aside the judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
3. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
4. Brief facts of the case are as under:
That on 24.04.2019 at about 9.30 a.m., the claimant was boarding the BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA- 57-F-2929 by holding the bus rod handle on Bengaluru- Sarjapura main road in front of Indian oil petrol bunk, NC: 2024:KHC:14950 Sarjapura, Bengaluru, the driver of the bus without observing the side mirror suddenly closed the bus door and moved ahead in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

entities.text: Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He was immediately shifted to Sparsh Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given.
Thereafter, to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital and later, to St.Johns Hospital, wherein, he took treatment as an inpatient for 15 days.
In view of injuries suffered and financial expenditure expended, he filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

4.1 On service of notice, respondent-Corporation appeared through its counsel and filed statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation, income and denied the negligence against the driver of the bus.
He also pleaded that the claimant was trying to board the moving bus from the road side and not in the bus stand and due to his negligence, he fell down and sustained injuries.
Therefore, the claimant himself was negligent and responsible for the NC: 2024:KHC:14950 occurrence of the accident and suffered injuries.
On these grounds, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4.2 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
4.3 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and the Doctor as PW.2 and one witness as PW.3 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P15.

On the other hand, respondent examined a witness as RW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
4.4

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.5,15,700/- with interest @ 7% p.a. and respondent-Corporation was directed to deposit the amount within two months.

3 NC: 2024:KHC:14950 4.5 The claimant as well as the Corporation being dissatisfied and aggrieved by the judgment and award are before this Court challenging the same on several grounds urged in their respective appeals.

sentences.text: 5. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Corporation contends that the award of the tribunal deserves to be set aside.
Hence, he seeks to allow his appeal.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for claimant and learned counsel for Corporation, perused the impugned judgment and award, it is seen that the claimant has produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P15, out of which, Exs.P1 to P4, P6 are the Police records, which clearly NC: 2024:KHC:14950 depict the filing of FIR and laying of charge sheet against the driver of the bus and same has not been challenged or controverted.
Therefore, the tribunal rightly attributed the negligence against the driver of the bus.

Exs.P5, P7 to P15 are the medical records and the salary slips etc.
8.

Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation, income and disability, it is stated that age of the claimant was 24 years as on the date of occurrence of accident and the tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '18', which does not call for interference.
The income has taken at Rs.15,000/- per month, though Ex.P7-Salary slip is produced to show Rs.22,000/-.
But, author has not been examined, the tribunal has taken the notional income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
I am in agreement with the learned counsel for Corporation that the income taken is on the higher side as the Legal Service Authority chart prescribes Rs.14,000/- for the accident year 2019.
Hence, the income is reduced to Rs.14,000/- per month as against Rs.15,000/-.
PW.2-Doctor has opined the disability to an extent of 17% to the left lower limb, but he has not assessed the disability to the whole body.
However, the tribunal has taken the disability at 10%.
I am afraid that the disability taken by the tribunal is erroneous as the injuries sustained by the claimant is only to the left lower limb.
Therefore, if it is divided by 1/3rd , the disability would be 5.6%, which is rounded off to 6%.
Hence, the disability to the whole body is taken at 6%.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to reduced compensation of Rs.1,81,440/- (Rs.14,000/- x 12 x 18 x 6%) towards loss of future income as against Rs.3,24,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
10. The tribunal awarded Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering.
However, I deem it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.20,000/-.

In all, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.40,000/-
under this head.
11. The tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges.
However, the claimant was inpatient for 15 days.

sentences.text: Therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.15,000/- under this head.
12. Towards medical expenses, Rs.1,26,700/- is awarded by the tribunal on the basis of actual bills produced by the claimant, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.
13. The tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
Considering the magnitude of injuries, the claimant would require atleast four months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.

Therefore, claimant would be entitled to Rs.56,000/-
(Rs.14,000/- x 4) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
14. The tribunal awarded Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.40,000/- under this head.
In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.4,59,140/- as against Rs.5,15,700/- as mentioned in the table below:

Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and suffering 40,000-00 Food and nourishment, conveyance 15,000-00 and attendant charges Medical expenses 1,26,700-00
Loss of income during the laid up 56,000-00 period
Loss of future income 1,81,440-00 Loss of amenities 40,000-00

Learned counsel for Corporation contends that the tribunal has awarded exorbitant interest which is not contemplated under the Motor Vehicles Act and the Rules and therefore, the same requires to be lowered as per Section 34 of CPC.
17.

I am in agreement with argument of learned counsel for Corporation that the Motor Vehicles Act and Rules do not prescribe the interest component and therefore, this Court has to revert to the Code of Civil Procedure wherein Section 34 prescribes 6% interest.
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:14950
Hence, it is appropriate to award interest at 6% as against 7% awarded by the tribunal.
